- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially after dips.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., 86.87 → 88.35) — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting — forecast should be adjusted upward 1–2 days early if sentiment turns bullish.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: if model is consistently above 85.0, reduce by 0.5–1.5% per day if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum — add 0.3–0.7% lagged momentum to forecast.
- Avoid linear extrapolation — if sentiment is volatile, use 3–5 day smoothing or sentiment-weighted average for horizon correction.
